Select groups of predictor variables

Source: R/predictor_groups.R
predictor_groups.Rd

Select non-overlapping groups of predictors using adaptive ridge and a group L0 penalty. Groups can represent factor contrasts, spline coefficients, related measurements or other terms that should enter a model together.

Arguments

group

Optional vector with one label per column of the supplied X, excluding an automatically added intercept. Factors, integers and character labels are accepted; ordering and consecutive numbering are unnecessary. Label 0 or "0" identifies unpenalized terms. Intercepts and always.include terms remain unpenalized. NULL uses individual predictors.

group.multiplier

Optional positive penalty multipliers, one per penalized predictor group in first-appearance order, or a named vector matching the nonzero group labels. A scalar applies to every group. By default, named IC presets charge each group's coefficient dimension; a numeric lambda charges once per group. Returned group.multiplier values reproduce the preset when reusing its numeric lambda. Tuning uses dimension-based multipliers throughout its path and training folds.

Value

Fits retain group, group.multiplier, eligible-entry masks and selected-block masks, together with the usual fit fields. Use the stored multipliers with a numeric lambda to reproduce an IC-preset or tuned fit.

Details

For working coefficients \(b_{jc}=s_j\beta_{jc}\) and predictor group \(G_g\), independent-channel selection (grouped=FALSE) uses $$r_{gc}^2=\sum_{j\in G_g}b_{jc}^2.$$ Joint selection (grouped=TRUE) uses $$r_g^2=\sum_c\sum_{j\in G_g}b_{jc}^2.$$ The norm prevents opposing signs from cancelling. Each penalized coefficient in a block receives ridge diagonal $$D_{jc}=\frac{\lambda a_g}{4r_g^2},$$ with the appropriate channel-specific norm for independent selection. Scalar GLM working weights are divided by the channel's dispersion, so this expression is on the likelihood scale. Equivalently, an unscaled weighted least-squares system multiplies the diagonal by dispersion. Adaptive weights use coefficients relative to zero; prior.mean remains the fixed ridge target.

The approximate selection target is $$-2\ell(B,\psi)+\lambda\sum_g a_g\,1(r_g>0),$$ with separate blocks per response when grouped=FALSE. A numeric lambda uses \(a_g=1\) by default. IC presets use the number of coefficients in the group, multiplied by the number of responses for joint selection. Joint multinomial groups use \((C-1)|G_g|\) dimensions for \(C\) CLR categories. Multinomial predictor groups require grouped=TRUE. Noise parameters and compulsory terms contribute to reported information criteria; their complexity charges are constant across group-support comparisons. Reported GIC, AIC and BIC count free nonzero coefficient entries, with the usual mandatory-term, noise-parameter and CLR adjustments. Group size is accounted for through these entries, without an additional size multiplier. When a retained group contains exact zeros, its reported parameter count can be smaller than the nominal group cost used in the adaptive-ridge update.

With zero ridge targets, the inverse-norm update is the quadratic majorization of a log-norm penalty. For an orthogonal block with curvature \(h\), its nonzero fixed point obeys \(r^2-\widehat r r+\lambda a_g/(4h)=0\); its existence boundary \(h\widehat r^2=\lambda a_g\) matches the block-L0 selection threshold. The relaxed refit removes shrinkage on selected blocks. Coefficients can be zero inside a retained group, for example at a nonnegative boundary.

Hard thresholding removes whole blocks using thresh and normalized norms. Explicit starting-zero exclusions remain binding for individual entries; intercepts and compulsory terms remain eligible. Structural zero columns do not enter solves. The returned sparse coefficient matrix retains the original predictor dimensions. group_support_size, group_df and group_objective in l0glmMetrics() describe the group fit, alongside coefficient-based scores.

Group models use the shared structured IRLS driver and the existing ridge solvers for ordinary GLMs, negative binomial, joint multinomial and Cox models. Predictor-group screening and outcome preclustering are unavailable; use screen="none" to fit a large group design directly. Local refinement tests additions, deletions and exchanges of complete predictor groups, accepting only improvements in the group objective (or supplied validation deviance). Named presets and tuning refine the reported parameter-count IC. Numeric penalties refine the weighted group-count objective; control.local$target can explicitly choose "IC" or "L0". Automatic refinement uses the selected coefficient-dimension limit described in local_search. Cholesky is used for regular systems; a rank-deficient unpenalized group refit can fall back to pivoted QR.

See also

l0glmFit(), l0nnPois(), l0glmTune(), l0glmMetrics()

Examples

set.seed(41)
X <- matrix(rnorm(200 * 12), 200, 12)
group <- rep(seq_len(6), each=2)
group[11:12] <- 0
beta <- c(1.5, -1.5, 0, 0, 1, -1, rep(0, 6))
y <- 1 + as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(200)
fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, group=group, lambda="gic", intercept=TRUE,
  relaxed=TRUE, local.search=FALSE)
l0glmMetrics(fit)[c("gic", "group_support_size", "group_df", "group_objective")]
same <- l0glmFit(X, y, group=group, lambda=fit$init.lambda,
  group.multiplier=fit$group.multiplier, intercept=TRUE,
  relaxed=TRUE, local.search=FALSE)
max(abs(coef(fit) - coef(same)))
